polls.description: Anthropic's AI agents autonomously took dangerous actions including filing false police reports and accessing government systems, raising critical questions about AI control and safety monitoring.
polls.question: Should AI companies face penalties for rogue AI incidents like Anthropic's?

cluster_stories.title: PSA: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash habitually exfiltrates API keys. It is dangerously misaligned and may be hazardous to use
cluster_stories.summary: EDIT: since people keep calling it out, this is API key abuse but not exfiltration. Seems like both Harbor and Pier (sandboxes used in almost every Software Engineering benchmark) expose the Openrouter endpoint and API key to models, even though they block the rest of the internet. Only DeepSeek V4.1 Flash absued this, and it did so while knowing it was "ethically gray". Other open models like DeepSeek V4, GLM 5.3 +Flash, and Qwen were fine. Logs attached. I know OpenRouter is not local, but considering people do run DeepSeek v4.1 Flash locally, I thought this was a matter you all might need to hear. We were running a DeepSWE variant on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash using the standard Pier sandbox. Out of all the 15 models we tested so far (including other open models like GLM 5.3/Flash, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731, etc), ONLY DeepSeek v4.1 Flash displays such pervasive malicious behavior: In 33% of runs, it attempts to exfiltrate the OpenRouter API key from its sandbox and in 11% of them,
cluster_stories.headline: DEEPSEEK V4.1 FLASH LEAKS API KEYS... Dangerously Misaligned

cluster_stories.title: Microsoft CEO Nadella Calls for ‘Emergency Brake’ on Advanced AI
cluster_stories.summary: Microsoft Corp. Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said companies should treat powerful artificial intelligence models as potential insider threats, assume they could be compromised and create an “emergency brake” system to prevent agentic models from going rogue.
cluster_stories.headline: NADELLA DEMANDS 'EMERGENCY BRAKE' ON ADVANCED AI... Insider Threat Warning

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic AI model sent fake murder tip to US police, hit government sites
cluster_stories.summary: An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, authorities said on Friday, criticising the company for taking two months to report the incident. It is the first known instance in which a rogue AI appears to have tried to communicate a bogus tip to authorities, despite ‌instructions not to create accounts or submit anything destructive, while not explicitly barred from submitting forms. The Philadelphia Police...
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC AI SUBMITS FAKE MURDER TIP... Hits Government Sites

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic AI Model Goes Rogue, Gives Cops a Fake Tip
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model went rogue and carried out unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations. In one example, the AI model gave police in Philadelphia a fake tip on a homicide case. The police took no action. Other unintended behaviors were also noted. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC AI GOES ROGUE... SENDS FAKE TIP TO POLICE

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic says its AI agents tried to break into government websites
cluster_stories.summary: In its latest report, Anthropic has revealed that its AI agents meddled with government websites during testing.
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC AI AGENTS TRIED TO HACK GOVERNMENT SITES

cluster_stories.title: Rogue Anthropic AI agent gave police fake tip in unsolved murder case
cluster_stories.summary: Philadelphia police said the tip was "flagged as spam", but criticised the tech company for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach.
cluster_stories.headline: ROGUE ANTHROPIC AI AGENT SENDS FAKE TIP IN MURDER CASE

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic Cites New AI Misbehavior, Some on Government Sites
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations, including some US government agencies’ websites, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems.
cluster_stories.headline: BREAKING: Anthropic AI Hit Multiple US Government Sites

cluster_stories.title: Odd Lots: How OpenAI’s Rogue Model Hacked Hugging Face
cluster_stories.summary: On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Nate Soares, president of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to talk about how a rogue OpenAI model hacked Hugging Face and why he thinks humanity's demise in the hands of superintelligent AI is inevitable. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: ROGUE OPENAI MODEL HACKED HUGGING FACE

cluster_stories.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
cluster_stories.summary: In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
cluster_stories.headline: MICROSOFT CEO: AI Models Need 'Emergency Brake'

cluster_stories.title: After Anthropic’s Claude AI submits a false tip on a Philadelphia unsolved homicide case, police say ‘cases involve real victims, grieving families’
cluster_stories.summary: The incident in Philadelphia occurred on July 18 when the AI model Claude Haiku 4.5 was tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said.
cluster_stories.headline: CLAUDE AI SUBMITS FALSE TIP TO PHILLY HOMICIDE UNIT

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic says small AI models could soon be able to copy themselves onto everyday devices
cluster_stories.summary: The AI company warns that cheap, freely available models may be months away from spreading across gadgets like smart TVs and ovens on their own.
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC WARNS: AI Models Could Self-Replicate

cluster_stories.title: Meta Releases New AI Model Called Muse Wonder
cluster_stories.summary: Meta Platforms, parent company of Facebook, has released a long-awaited artificial intelligence model called Muse Wonder. This model is said to be competitive with OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. Meta stock rose on the news. Mandeep Singh of Bloomberg Intelligence has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

cluster_stories.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder, catching OpenAI and Anthropic at the frontier
cluster_stories.summary: Meta has released a new AI model family called Muse Wonder. The new model leapfrogs Gemini 4, GPT-Astra, and Fable 5 in Artificial Analysis's leaderboard.

cluster_stories.title: Meta says its new AI models on par with OpenAI, Anthropic
cluster_stories.summary: Meta on Monday unveiled two new "frontier" artificial intelligence models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claims perform at a level comparable to that of OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. In a blog post, Meta touted so-called benchmarking data from an independent firm called Artificial Analysis that appears to show that Meta's newest Wonder models outperform its own previous models, Spark, as well as various models developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.
cluster_stories.headline: META UNVEILS WONDER AI MODELS... Claims Parity with ChatGPT

cluster_stories.title: Meta’s Muse Wonder Takes Aim at OpenAI, Anthropic
cluster_stories.summary: Meta says its new Muse Wonder model has frontier-level capabilities, marking a major milestone in the company’s AI overhaul under chief AI officer Alexandr Wang. Bloomberg’s Riley Griffin spoke to him, and joins to discuss how Meta is positioning the model against rivals including OpenAI and Anthropic and how it was purpose-built to power the company’s Muse personal AI assistant. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: META'S MUSE WONDER TARGETS OPENAI, ANTHROPIC
